messages:
lucy: quick sync on API keys list UX. main asks: make empty state actionable, reduce visual noise for long scope lists, and clarify ephemeral key lifecycle. attaching quick sketches: https://figma.com/file/abc (sketch A)
raj: for empty state I suggest a two-column layout: left explainer + CTA, right quick examples of common scope combos. keeps new users from guessing.
sam: agree. also add a tiny checklist under CTA: '1) name key 2) select scopes 3) copy value'. users often miss the copy step.
nora: accessibility: ensure the checklist is semantic (ol/li), not just visuals. screen readers need to navigate steps. include an aria-describedby on the modal pointing to the checklist.
lucy: good call. next: scope overflow. some orgs have 10+ scopes. option A: compact tokenized chips with overflow counter (+3). option B: collapsed summary like "8 scopes selected" with disclosure.
raj: prefer chips for discoverability, but we must prevent horizontal wrapping breaking row height. chips should truncate and show tooltip with full list.
sam: implementation: make chips non-focusable; the row should have a single "Show scopes" button that opens a popup with keyboard-focusable list.
nora: that handles keyboard users. popup needs role="dialog" and focus trap. also ensure esc closes and focus returns to the show button.
lucy: ephemeral keys: current flow uses a toast for TTL. proposed: show an expiry pill in the row + an optional bell icon to pin reminder. if pinned, create calendar reminder or email.
raj: backend note: we can expose TTL in the create response. front-end can render pill with relative time (e.g., "expires in 45m"). also show a progress bar for the first minute.
sam: microcopy for reveal: suggestion: "Key visible for 30s. Copy now." also show a copy button that updates to 'Copied!' for 2s and announces via aria-live polite.
nora: crucial accessibility piece: when the key is revealed, redact parts when screen reader is present unless the user confirms with a second explicit action. we should prompt: 'Confirm reveal for screen reader users'.
lucy: interesting—could be a toggle in preferences. for now, add a confirmation checkbox in the reveal dialog: 'I understand this key will be visible to anyone at my screen.'
raj: revoke flow: request adding optional 'reason' dropdown + freeform note. add small privacy hint: notes stored in audit logs and visible to admins only.
sam: audit log schema: add fields revoker_id, reason_code, note, timestamp. front-end will POST note to /api/keys/:id/revoke.
nora: make sure audit log entries are exposed in admin timeline with semantic headings and not inlined as blobs.
lucy: mobile: actions should collapse into a single affordance. suggestion: primary action is 'Copy' then kebab for others. also avoid tiny touch targets for revoke.
raj: design tweak: use a ghost 'Copy' button at start of row so it's always visible. safer than burying it. other actions in kebab.
sam: small UI nit: sorting by 'last used' vs 'created' should be persistent per user. add localStorage flag.
nora: accessibility note: ensure sort control is a <button> with aria-pressed states, not a plain link.
lucy: tasks from this thread: 1) lucy to update figma with empty-state and chips + collapsed summary variants, 2) sam to spec keyboard/focus behavior and aria strings, 3) raj to add TTL + revoke note fields to backend spec, 4) nora to review confirm-reveal wording for a11y. I'll file acceptance criteria after review. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: heads up: UI feature-flag 'keys_ui_v2' will gate the rollout. merge window target: 2026-04-05. include accessibility review before rollout.
lucy: thanks all, linking ticket: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/K-3212-keys-empty-state-ux
